standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the degree function of a normalized dualizing complex over a local ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 3524-3527)
standard_prerequisites.use: Relates the degrees at the two primes through the dimension of the local ring at the larger prime.

core_obligations: Reduce: replacing the ring by the quotient by the smaller prime, the dualizing complex by the internal hom out of that quotient and the primes accordingly, one may assume the ring is a domain, the smaller prime is zero and the larger prime has height one (proof lines 3506-3514)

Generic degree: by the nonvanishing statement exactly one cohomology module of the localized complex is nonzero, and its degree is the negative of the value of the function at the zero ideal, because shifting by that value makes the localized complex normalized over the fraction field (proof lines 3517-3521)

Special degree: shifting the localization at the larger prime by the negative of the value of the function there makes it normalized over the local ring at that prime, and the cited description of the nonzero degree over the quotient by the maximal ideal shows that over the fraction field the only nonzero degree is the negative dimension, which is minus one; comparing the two expressions gives the asserted additivity (proof lines 3524-3537)
proof_roadmap: 先把情形化归为 A 是域、p = (0)、q 高 1（商去 p，ω 换成 RHom(A/p, ω)，用 quotient-function 引理）。
由 nonvanishing-generically：(ω_A^•)_{(0)} 只在唯一 i_0 非零，且 i_0 = -δ((0))。
由 nonvanishing-generically-local：(ω_A^•)_q[-δ(q)] 在 (0) 处只在 e = -dim(A_q) = -1 非零 ⇒ H^{e-δ(q)}(ω_A^•)_{(0)} 唯一非零 ⇒ -δ((0)) = -1 - δ(q)，即 δ(p) = δ(q) + 1。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement says that the degree function defined by a dualizing complex on a Noetherian ring is a dimension function, i.e. that it drops by exactly one along an immediate specialization (author lemma at source lines 3497-3503, label lemma-dimension-function). The proof (source lines 3505-3538) first reduces to a domain with the smaller prime equal to zero and the larger prime of height one, then identifies the unique nonvanishing degree of the localization at the generic point with the negative value of the function there, and compares it with the normalized description at the larger prime, where the only nonzero degree over the fraction field is minus the dimension, which is minus one (proof lines 3524-3537). The comparison of the two normalizations is the substance. H3.
